title: Google Assistant will vanish from Android phones and connected devices in September
excerpt: Google is retiring Assistant across phones, Wear OS watches, cars and connected devices in September, replacing a decade-old voice interaction model with Gemini. The largest forced assistant-UX migration yet across consumer hardware.
rationale: A hard September deadline that rewrites the voice layer on every Android phone, watch, car and speaker — the biggest interaction-model swap designers have to plan around this year.

title: Siri AI is coming to newer Apple devices only, here's the full list
excerpt: Apple published the hardware matrix for Siri AI across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Watch and Vision Pro, and older devices are cut. On-device model requirements are now openly fragmenting the install base.
rationale: The official device cut-list turns on-device AI into a hardware tier — anyone designing an Apple-side feature now has to design the fallback for excluded devices.

title: Google quietly rewrote Chrome's AI documentation with important answers to on-device AI downloads
excerpt: Chrome's updated help pages finally spell out what on-device AI costs your machine, including roughly 20GB of free disk space for the local model. The hidden hardware tax of browser-resident AI, in writing.
rationale: Puts a number on the local-AI tax — ~20GB of disk before the browser will run a model — which is the constraint every on-device web feature has to budget for.

title: Nothing is using AI-generated people to show off its new earbuds – everyone hates it
excerpt: Nothing's CMF launched the Clip Pro earbuds with AI-generated models in its product imagery, and the backlash swamped the launch. A live case study in the credibility cost of synthetic product photography.
rationale: A design-led brand losing its launch narrative to synthetic imagery — the clearest evidence yet of where AI-generated assets break audience trust.

title: Peloton Cross Training Bike+ review: A better connected bike that still demands a premium price
excerpt: Peloton's new bike builds an AI tracking camera into the hardware so the machine can watch and coach your form. A concrete example of computer vision moving from app feature to built-in product surface.
rationale: A shipping product where computer vision stops being an app feature and becomes built-in hardware — a usable reference for embedding a camera-as-coach into physical design.
